title: Make the content of zedu.chat/solutions readable without JavaScript, by Fri 13 Nov
description:
Checked on 22 Oct 2026: the HTML of zedu.chat/solutions holds about 8 words of text and no H1 or images (the home page holds about 900 words, pricing about 400). A crawler that doesn't run JavaScript sees almost nothing on this page.

Success looks like: the page's headings and body text are in the HTML the server sends (check with curl, not a browser), the word count is in line with the other marketing pages, and the page still looks the same to visitors. Say which fix was used (server rendering, static rendering or other) and which file it touched in zedu-fe.

acceptedWorkstreams.description: Confirmed 22 Oct 2026: curl of zedu.chat/solutions gives about 8 words and no H1, while /solutions/bootcamps, /schools and /universities each serve 390-440 words. tasks.title: Add a server-rendered /solutions hub page, with before/after curl evidence

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Scope it correctly: the index page is the only empty one - the three detail pages already serve 2,100-3,300 words
acceptedWorkstreams.description:
Measured today with curl (22 Oct 2026), no browser: /solutions returns 0 H1, 0 H2 and 8 visible words - matching the goal's finding exactly. But the three pages linked from it are healthy on the same test: /solutions/bootcamps 3,034 visible characters, /solutions/schools 2,794, /solutions/universities 3,347, each with a real H1 and full heading structure in the server HTML.

That changes the shape of the fix, and it is worth stating before anyone rebuilds the branch: the text and the server rendering already work on the detail pages, so whatever is wrong is specific to the /solutions index route - the accepted approaches point at it having no page file and falling into the app shell, which fits what the HTML shows (a document shell with no content markup at all).

Deliverables:
1) The measurement table: every solutions URL with visible word count, H1 and H2 counts, taken with curl on the delivery date, so the scope is evidence rather than assumption.
2) The fix for the index route only, with the zedu-fe file touched, and the check re-run showing the index word count in line with the detail pages.
3) A guard for the future: a one-command check anyone can run (curl, strip tags, count words and headings) that fails if a public page falls below the site's normal range - so an empty page is caught the next time a route is added, not by a reviewer.
4) An honest limit: a static fetch cannot tell whether interactive parts (accordions, tabbed content) need JavaScript, so anything that looks missing gets flagged for a browser check rather than guessed at.

This narrows rather than duplicates the two accepted approaches - both are aimed at the index route, and this adds the proof that the rest of the branch is already fine plus the check that keeps it that way.
